# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

We pledge to make our community welcoming, safe, and 
equitable for all.

We as members, contributors, and maintainers are committed 
to fostering an open and welcoming environment that 
makes participation in our project and our community a 
harassment-free experience, that respects and promotes the 
dignity, rights, and contributions of all individuals, 
regardless of characteristics including race, ethnicity, 
caste, color, age, physical characteristics, 
neurodiversity, visible or invisible disability, sex, 
sex characteristics, sexual identity, sexual orientation, 
gender identity, or gender expression, language, 
philosophy or religion, national or social origin, 
socio-economic status or position, level of education, or 
other status. The same privileges of participation are 
extended to everyone who participates in good faith and in 
accordance with this Covenant.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to 
an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy 
community.

## Our Standards

### Encouraged Behaviors
While acknowledging differences in social norms, we all 
strive to meet our community's expectations for positive 
behavior. We also understand that our words and actions 
may be interpreted differently than we intend based on 
culture, background, or native language.

With these considerations in mind, we agree to behave 
mindfully toward each other and act in ways that center 
our shared values.

**Examples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:**

1. Using welcoming and inclusive language.
2. Respecting the **purpose of our community**, our 
    activities, and our ways of gathering.
3. Engaging **kindly and honestly** with others, 
    demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people.
4. Respecting **different viewpoints**, opinions, and 
    experiences.
5. **Taking responsibility** for our actions and 
    contributions, and apologizing to those affected by our 
    mistakes, and learning from the experience.
6. Gracefully giving and accepting 
    **constructive feedback**.
7. Committing to **repairing harm** when it occurs.
8. Behaving in other ways that promote and sustain the 
    **well-being of our community**.
9. Discuss technical proposals rigorously while directing 
    criticism at ideas, code, designs, and evidence—not at 
    the people presenting them.

### Restricted Behaviors
We agree to restrict the following behaviors in our 
community. Instances, threats, and promotion of these 
behaviors are violations of this Code of Conduct.

**Examples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:**

1. **Harassment.** Violating explicitly expressed 
    boundaries or engaging in unnecessary personal 
    attention after any clear request to stop.
2. **Personal attacks.** Insulting, trolling, demeaning, 
    or pejorative comments directed at a community member 
    or group of people, including attacks based on 
    protected characteristics.
3. **Stereotyping or discrimination.** Characterizing, 
    excluding, or mistreating anyone on the basis of 
    protected characteristics or status.
4. **Sexualization.** Using sexualized language or 
    imagery, making unwelcome sexual attention or advances, 
    or behaving in a way that would generally be considered 
    inappropriately intimate for the context or purpose of 
    the community.
5. **Violating confidentiality.** Sharing or acting on 
    someone's personal or private information without 
    their explicit permission.
6. **Endangerment.** Causing, encouraging, or threatening 
    violence or other harm toward any person or group.
7. Behaving in other ways that **threaten the well-being** 
    of our community.
8. Other conduct which could reasonably be considered 
    inappropriate in a professional setting.
9. Repeated bad-faith disruption of technical discussion, 
    including deliberate misrepresentation of another 
    participant’s position or persistent derailment after 
    moderator direction.

### Other Restrictions

1. **Misleading identity.** Impersonating someone else 
    for any reason, or pretending to be someone else to 
    evade enforcement actions.
2. **Attribution and licensing.** Misrepresenting 
    authorship, removing required attribution or license 
    notices, or contributing third-party material without 
    complying with its applicable license or attribution 
    requirements.
3. **Promotional materials.** Sharing marketing or other 
    commercial content in a way that is outside the norms 
    of the community.
4. **Promotion of harmful conduct.** Endorsing, encouraging, 
    or materially facilitating restricted behavior, except 
    where reasonably necessary for reporting, moderation, 
    security research, documentation, education, or other 
    legitimate project purposes.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, 
and also applies when an individual is officially 
representing the community in public or other spaces. 
Examples of representing our community include using an 
official email address, posting via an official social 
media account, or acting as an appointed representative at 
an online or offline event.

Representation of a project may be further defined and 
clarified by the Community Moderators.

## Our Responsibilities

The project maintainers are the Community Moderators unless 
the project publicly designates additional moderators.

Community Moderators are responsible for clarifying and enforcing 
our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate 
and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that 
they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community Moderators have the right and responsibility to remove, 
edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, 
and other contributions that are not aligned to this 
Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation
decisions when appropriate.

## Enforcement

Tensions can occur between community members even when they 
are trying their best to collaborate. Not every conflict 
represents a Code of Conduct violation. This Code of Conduct 
reinforces encouraged behaviors and norms that can help 
avoid conflicts and minimize harm.

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be
reported privately to the Community Moderators at
[report@dragonstone-lang.org](mailto:report@dragonstone-lang.org).

If a report concerns a Community Moderator, or if the reporter is
uncomfortable using the primary reporting channel, they may contact the
project owner at
[v@dragonstone-lang.org](mailto:v@dragonstone-lang.org).

A Community Moderator with a conflict of interest will not 
participate in reviewing or deciding that report. If a 
report concerns the project owner, the project will 
appoint an independent temporary reviewer or seek 
confidential assistance from a trusted external maintainer.

Community Moderators take reports of violations seriously. 
Reports will be reviewed and investigated promptly and 
fairly. Community Moderators will make every effort to 
respond in a timely manner. Enforcement actions are 
ordinarily carried out privately with the involved parties. 
Communication to the broader community may occur when 
necessary to protect the community or as part of a mutually 
agreed resolution. All Community Moderators are obligated to 
maintain confidentiality and to respect the privacy and 
security of reporters, witnesses, and other affected people.

Community Moderators who do not follow or enforce the Code 
of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent 
repercussions as determined by other members of the 
community’s leadership.

> Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.

## Possible Enforcement Actions

Moderators will consider the severity, frequency, intent, 
and impact of a violation, and any prior violations when 
determining an appropriate action. Actions may include a 
private warning; content removal or editing; limits on 
participation; temporary suspension from project spaces; 
or permanent removal from project spaces. Community 
Moderators may skip steps where necessary to protect 
community safety.
